subject: Stan slower on Debian than OSX

messages.author: 32bf4f27a31a68db
messages.subject: Stan slower on Debian than OSX
parts:
I've been using Stan (through rstan) for a long time on OSX.  Works great.

Recently acquired a second machine, and decided to dedicate it to Stan work. (Can then use all the CPU cores for long running sampling projects.)

It has
  •  i7 CPU
  • 32 GB RAM
  • Debian 8
  • g++ 4.92

For some strange reason, Stan sampling runs SLOW on the Debian machine.  Maybe 1/10 of the speed as on the OSX machine.  Since the hardware is similar, my guess is that is is related to a software library or dependency somewhere.

Does anybody have any suggestions as to why this might be, or what to look for?


Thanks!

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Stan slower on Debian than OSX
parts:
Hi Noah,

First, which Stan interface are you using? I'd try running CmdStan first to get rid of the interaction with any of the computing platforms. 

How do the effective sample sizes look? Are they similar? 

I'd try these things:
- change compiler optimization level
- change compiler version
- change compiler (OS X now defaults to clang++)
- make sure to time only the run and not the compile time (compile times vary widely with compilers, versions, and optimization levels)

And I would be very careful about measuring N_eff / s and using that as my comparison instead of wall time. Seeds aren't going to reproduce the same results across platforms (it will reproduce the same results on the same platform with the same compiler, compiler settings, and version of Stan), so comparing behavior for particular seeds isn't a great comparison. 

Can you let us know if you find anything useful? (Or even if you dont?)


Daniel
